answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work. Agents trading quartz, tending lotus ponds, or monitoring river levels face the same rule, and each additional identity needs its own deposit. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing financing costs and lost investment opportunities. The defense makes identities costly without pretending to prove who owns them.
